text:
For $\mathrm{A}_{2}+\mathrm{B}_{2}⇌2\mathrm{AB}$

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$ for forward and backward reaction are 180 and $200\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively

If catalyst lowers $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$ for both reactions by $100\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction.
The enthalpy change for the reaction is $+20\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
Catalyst can cause non-spontaneous reactions to occur.
The enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction is different from that of uncatalysed reaction.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the uncatalysed reaction, $\Delta H=E_{a,f}-E_{a,b}=180-200=-20\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, so statement (B) is false.

With the catalyst, $E_{a,f}=180-100=80\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $E_{a,b}=200-100=100\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, giving $\Delta H=80-100=-20\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, the same as before, so (D) is false.

A catalyst lowers the activation energies of the forward and backward reactions equally and does not change the energies of the reactants and products. Hence $\Delta H$ and $\Delta G$ of the reaction are unaltered, so (A) is true.

Since $\Delta G$ is unaltered, a reaction with $\Delta G>0$ cannot be made spontaneous by a catalyst, so (C) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

Predict the major product of the following reaction sequence:-

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Free-radical bromination ($\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}/hν$) is highly selective for the hydrogen whose removal gives the most stable radical. The ring carbon bearing $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ gives a $3^{\circ }$ radical, so the product is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.

Alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ on heating removes $\mathrm{HBr}$; by Saytzeff's rule the more substituted alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene, is formed.

$\mathrm{HBr}$ in the presence of peroxide adds by a free-radical path: $\mathrm{Br}^{\bullet }$ adds to C-2 so that the more stable $3^{\circ }$ radical forms at C-1, which then takes H from $\mathrm{HBr}$. The product is 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane (anti-Markovnikov addition).


[IMG]

Without peroxide, Markovnikov addition would instead give 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane, structure (A).

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Which one of the following about an electron occupying the 1 s orbital in a hydrogen atom is incorrect?

(Bohr's radius is represented by $\mathrm{a}_{0}$)
options: The probability density of finding the electron is maximum at the nucleus
The total energy of the electron is maximum when it is at a distance $a_{0}$ from the nucleus
The electron can be found at a distance $2a_{0}$ from the nucleus
The 1 s orbital is spherically symmetrical
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the $1s$ orbital the probability density $ψ^{2}$ is greatest at the nucleus and falls off exponentially with distance $r$:


[IMG]

(A) The probability density is maximum at the nucleus ($r=0$), so (A) is correct.

(B) An electron in the $1s$ orbital has a fixed total energy, $E_{1}=-13.6\text{eV}$, which does not change with its distance from the nucleus. The quantity that is maximum at $a_{0}$ is the radial probability $4πr^{2}ψ^{2}$, not the energy, so (B) is incorrect.

(C) $ψ^{2}$ is non-zero at every finite distance, so the electron can be found at $2a_{0}$; (C) is correct.

(D) The $1s$ wave function depends only on $r$, so the orbital is spherically symmetrical; (D) is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: On charging the lead storage battery, the oxidation state of lead changes from $x_{1}$ to $y_{1}$ at the anode and from $x_{2}$ to $y_{2}$ at the cathode. The values of $x_{1},y_{1},x_{2},y_{2}$ are respectively :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For charging of lead storage battery cell reaction is

$2\mathrm{PbSO}_{4}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\to \mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{PbO}_{2}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}(\mathrm{aq})$

The question names the plates by their role during discharge, as NCERT does: the Pb plate is called the anode and the $\mathrm{PbO}_{2}$ plate the cathode. On charging, the discharge reactions are reversed at these same plates:

At anode (Pb plate) $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4}$ is reduced back to Pb and at cathode ($\mathrm{PbO}_{2}$ plate) $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4}$ is oxidised back to $\mathrm{PbO}_{2}$.

(In an electrolytic cell oxidation occurs at the anode, so by that strict naming the two plates swap names while charging; the options here follow the discharge names. Option A, $0,+2,+4,+2$, is the discharge process, not charging.)

$\begin{array}{ll} \because  & \mathrm{x}_{1}=+2,\mathrm{y}_{1}=0 \\ \mathrm{x}_{2} & =+2,\mathrm{y}_{2}=+4 \end{array}$

text: Aldol condensation is a popular and classical method to prepare $α,β$-unsaturated carbonyl compounds. This reaction can be both intermolecular and intramolecular. Predict which one of the following is not a product of intramolecular aldol condensation?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an intramolecular aldol condensation the enolate carbon and the carbonyl carbon belong to the same molecule, so the new $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$, formed between the $α$-carbon and the former carbonyl carbon, lies inside the newly formed ring.

(B), 2-methylene-1-tetralone, has a terminal exocyclic $=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$. That $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ was a carbonyl carbon bonded to no other carbon, that is formaldehyde, so (B) arises only from an intermolecular (crossed) aldol of 1-tetralone with $\mathrm{HCHO}$.

The others are ring-closure products: (A) from cyclodecane-1,5-dione (transannular closure giving the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ at the ring fusion), (C) cyclohex-2-en-1-one from 5-oxohexanal, and (D) inden-1-one from 2-acetylbenzaldehyde.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Which one of the following complexes will have $\Delta _{\mathrm{o}}=0$ and $μ=5.96$ B.M?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an octahedral complex, $\text{CFSE}=(-0.4n_{t_{2g}}+0.6n_{e_{g}})\Delta _{o}$ and $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M., where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons. The condition "$\Delta _{o}=0$" means a crystal field stabilisation energy of zero.

In $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{4-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{6}$ and $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so the configuration is $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ with $n=4$.


[IMG]

$μ=\sqrt{24}=4.90\text{B.M.},\text{CFSE}=(-0.4\times 4+0.6\times 2)\Delta _{o}=-0.4\Delta _{o}$

In $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{SCN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$, $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{5}$ and $\mathrm{SCN}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so the configuration is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ with $n=5$.


[IMG]

$μ=\sqrt{35}=5.92\text{B.M.},\text{CFSE}=(-0.4\times 3+0.6\times 2)\Delta _{o}=0$

In $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is a strong field ligand for $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, so the configuration is $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, giving $μ=0$ and $\text{CFSE}=-2.4\Delta _{o}$.

In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{6}$ and $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, so the configuration is also $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, giving $μ=0$ and $\text{CFSE}=-2.4\Delta _{o}$.


[IMG]

Only $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{SCN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$ has zero CFSE and five unpaired electrons, with $μ\approx 5.9$ B.M., the value quoted as 5.96 B.M.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
Number of stereoisomers possible for the complexes, $[\mathrm{CrCl}_{3}(\mathrm{py})_{3}]$ and $[\mathrm{CrCl}_{2}(\mathrm{ox})_{2}]^{3-}$ are respectively
$(py=$ pyridine,$ox=$ oxalate $)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{3}(\mathrm{py}){}_{3}]$ is an octahedral $\mathrm{Ma}_{3}\mathrm{b}_{3}$ complex with two geometrical isomers: fac (three Cl on one face) and mer (three Cl along one meridian). Both have a mirror plane, so neither is optically active: 2 stereoisomers.

$[\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{ox}){}_{2}]{}^{3-}$ is an octahedral $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA})_{2}\mathrm{b}_{2}$ complex. The trans isomer (Cl at $180^{\circ }$) has a mirror plane and is optically inactive. The cis isomer (Cl at $90^{\circ }$) is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers. Total: $1+2=3$ stereoisomers.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: An organic compound $(\mathrm{X})$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{6}\mathrm{O}$ is not readily oxidised. On reduction it gives $\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{8}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{Y})$ which reacts with HBr to give a bromide $(\mathrm{Z})$ which is converted to Grignard reagent. This Grignard reagent on reaction with $(\mathrm{X})$ followed by hydrolysis gives 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. Compounds $(\mathrm{X}),(\mathrm{Y})$ and $(\mathrm{Z})$ respectively are:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A compound $\mathrm{C}{}_{3}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}\mathrm{O}$ that is not readily oxidised is the ketone acetone, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$ (X); its isomer propanal would be oxidised easily.

Reduction of X gives propan-2-ol, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (Y), and HBr converts Y into 2-bromopropane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Br})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (Z).

Z with Mg in dry ether gives $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHMgBr}$, which adds to the C=O of acetone; hydrolysis gives $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, which is 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (B).

Let us consider a reversible reaction at temperature, T.

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{G}<0 \\ \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T}\Delta \mathrm{S}<0 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}>\left (\dfrac{\Delta \mathrm{H}}{\Delta \mathrm{S}}\right )=\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{e}} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}>\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{e}} \end{array}$

text:
Which of the following molecule(s) show/s paramagnetic behavior?

A. $\mathrm{O}_{2}$

B. $\mathrm{N}_{2}$

C. $\mathrm{F}_{2}$

D. $\mathrm{S}_{2}$

E. $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A molecule is paramagnetic when it has unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (16 electrons): $\mathrm{KK}(σ2s)^{2}(σ^{\ast }2s)^{2}(σ2p_{z})^{2}(π2p_{x})^{2}(π2p_{y})^{2}(π^{\ast }2p_{x})^{1}(π^{\ast }2p_{y})^{1}$, so it has 2 unpaired electrons and is paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{S}{}_{2}$ has the same 12 valence electrons as $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, with one electron in each of the two degenerate $π^{\ast }3p$ orbitals, so it also has 2 unpaired electrons and is paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ (bond order 3), $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ (bond order 1) have all their electrons paired, so they are diamagnetic.

The paramagnetic molecules are A and D.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Identify the pair of reactants that upon reaction, with elimination of HCl will give rise to the dipeptide Gly-Ala.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the dipeptide Gly-Ala, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{COOH}$, the carbonyl group of glycine is joined to the nitrogen of alanine.

So glycine must supply the acid chloride, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COCl}$, and alanine must supply a free nucleophilic $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ group; the amide bond forms with elimination of $\mathrm{HCl}$:

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{COOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{HCl}$

In (A) there is no $-\mathrm{COCl}$ group, so $\mathrm{HCl}$ cannot be eliminated; in (B) the alanine nitrogen is $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}{}^{+}$ with no lone pair; in (D) the $-\mathrm{COCl}$ belongs to alanine, which would give Ala-Gly.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Given below are the pairs of group 13 elements showing their relation in terms of atomic radius. $(\mathrm{B}<\mathrm{Al}),(\mathrm{Al}<\mathrm{Ga}),(\mathrm{Ga}<\mathrm{In})$ and $(\mathrm{In}<\mathrm{Tl})$

Identify the elements present in the incorrect pair and in that pair find out the element (X) that has higher ionic radius $\left (\mathrm{M}^{3+}\right )$ than the other one. The atomic number of the element $(\mathrm{X})$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Atomic radii of group 13 elements (pm): B 85, Al 143, Ga 135, In 167, Tl 170.

Gallium follows the ten $3d$ electrons, which shield the nuclear charge poorly; its larger effective nuclear charge makes Ga smaller than Al. Hence the pair $(\mathrm{Al}<\mathrm{Ga})$ is incorrect, while the other three pairs are correct.

For the trivalent ions of this pair, $\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$ ($1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}$) has two shells and a radius of 53.5 pm, while $\mathrm{Ga}{}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}$) has three shells and a radius of 62 pm.

$r(\mathrm{Ga}{}^{3+})>r(\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+})\Rightarrow \mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Ga}$

The atomic number of Ga is 31.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
$XY$ is the membrane/partition between two chambers 1 and 2 containing sugar solutions of concentration $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}(c_{1}>c_{2})\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$. For the reverse osmosis to take place identify the correct condition.

(Here $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$ are pressures applied on chamber 1 and 2 ).


[IMG]


A. Membrane/Partition : Cellophane, $\mathrm{p}_{1}>π$

B. Membrane/Partition : Porous, $\mathrm{p}_{2}>π$

C. Membrane/Partition : Parchment paper, $p_{1}>π$

D. Membrane/Partition : Cellophane, $\mathrm{p}_{2}>π$

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Chambers 1 and 2 hold sugar solutions with $c_{1}>c_{2}$, so in normal osmosis the solvent (water) flows through the semipermeable membrane from the dilute chamber 2 into the concentrated chamber 1.


[IMG]

Reverse osmosis drives the solvent the other way, from chamber 1 to chamber 2. This needs a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure applied on the more concentrated side, so $p_{1}>π$. A pressure on chamber 2 ($p_{2}>π$) only pushes the solvent further in the normal direction.

The partition must be semipermeable, letting water through but not sugar. Cellophane and parchment paper are semipermeable membranes, whereas a porous partition lets the sugar pass as well, so neither osmosis nor reverse osmosis occurs across it.

Thus statements A and C are correct, while B and D are not.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: The pH of a 0.01 M weak acid $\mathrm{HX}\left (\mathrm{K}_{a}=4\times 10^{-10}\right )$ is found to be 5 . Now the acid solution is diluted with excess of water so that the pH of the solution changes to 6 . The new concentration of the diluted weak acid is given as $x\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{M}$. The value of $x$ is $_________ ($nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}$ does not change on dilution, so use the given $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}$ with the pH after dilution.

$\mathrm{HX}_{(\mathrm{aq})}⇌\mathrm{H}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+}+\mathrm{X}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{-}\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=4\times 10^{-10}$

After dilution, pH $=6$, so $[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=[\mathrm{X}^{-}]=10^{-6}\mathrm{M}$. Let the new concentration of the acid be $\mathrm{C}$ M.

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}} & =\dfrac{[\mathrm{H}^{+}][\mathrm{X}^{-}]}{\mathrm{C}-[\mathrm{H}^{+}]} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{C} & =\dfrac{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}}+[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=\dfrac{10^{-12}}{4\times 10^{-10}}+10^{-6} \\ \qquad =25\times 10^{-4}+0.01\times 10^{-4}=25.01\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{M} \end{array}$

Therefore, $x=25$ (nearest integer).

Note: the statement that the 0.01 M acid has pH 5 does not fit the given $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}$. With $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=4\times 10^{-10}$, $[\mathrm{H}^{+}]\approx \sqrt{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}\times 0.01}=2\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{M}$, i.e. pH $\approx 5.7$. That statement is not used in the calculation, and NTA's final answer key gives 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen 1 g of an organic compound gave 150 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 900 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is $_______$ % (nearest integer)

(Aqueous tension at $300\mathrm{K}=15\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{N}_{2}=(900-15)=885\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$

Mole of $\mathrm{N}_{2}=\frac{\left (\frac{885}{760}\times 0.15\right )}{(0.0821\times 300)}=0.0071$ moles

$%$ of nitrogen in organic compound

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{(0.0071\times 28)}{1}\times 10 \\ =19.85% \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
Fortification of food with iron is done using $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot 7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. The mass in grams of the $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot 7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ required to achieve 12 ppm of iron in 150 kg of wheat is $______ ($Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{S}$ and O respectively are 56, 32 and $16\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let mass of iron $=\mathrm{w}g$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{w}}{150\times 10^{3}}\times 10^{6}=12 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=150\times 12\times 10^{-3}=1.8\mathrm{gm} \end{array}$

Let mass of $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot 7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{w}_{1}\mathrm{gm}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \text{Moles of}\mathrm{Fe}=\dfrac{1.8}{56}=\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{w}_{1}}{56+96+7\times 18}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{w}_{1}=8.935\mathrm{gm} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. ' X ' is the difference between the oxidation states of Mn in reactant and product. ' Y ' is the number of ' d ' electrons present in the brown red precipitate formed at the end of the acetate ion test with neutral ferric chloride. The value of $\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


X is difference in oxidation state.

$7-2=5$

So $X=5$

$\begin{array}{l} 6\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COO}^{⊖}+3\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \\ \to [\mathrm{Fe}_{3}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COO})_{6}]^{⊕}+2\mathrm{H}^{⊕} \\ [\mathrm{Fe}_{3}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COO})_{6}]^{⊕}+4\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \\ \to [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COO}]_{\text{Brown red ppt}}+\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{H}^{⊕} \end{array}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\Rightarrow 3\mathrm{d}^{5}4\mathrm{s}^{0}$ contains 5 d electrons

So $Y=5$

$X+Y=5+5=10$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
The total number of hydrogen bonds of a DNA-double Helix strand whose one strand has the following sequence of bases is $________$.

$5^{'}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{A}-3^{'}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Two nucleic acid chains are wound about each other and held together by H bonds between pair of bases.

Adenine from two hydrogen bonds with thymine and Guanine form three hydrogen bond with cytosine.

$5^{'}\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{A}-3^{'}$

In given DNA strand total seven guanine and cytosine bases which form total 21 H -bonds and six adenine and thymine base which will form total 12 H -bonds with other DNA strand.

Total no. of H bonds $=7\times 3+6\times 2=33$

Ans. 33
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift
